expected_answer.conclusion: The metadata supports explicit ID-to-method associations within each group and two thermo–orbital method/solvent matches. It does not prove shared cross-property calculation provenance. Vibration has a different basis set, and its water entry is unavailable in these results. Numerical residuals remain unavailable—not zero—because no numerical calculation outputs were observed.

explicit_links.finding: Each returned property ID can be associated with its level of theory by the identical source label in that group's ID and method maps.
Both explicitly report wB97M-V/def2-TZVPPD/VACUUM for this molecule. This is a method-and-environment match, not proof of a shared calculation; their property IDs differ.
Both explicitly report wB97M-V/def2-TZVPPD/SMD under SOLVENT=WATER. This is a method-and-solvent match, not proof of a shared calculation; their property IDs differ.

field_and_context_status.NONE: An actual source-map label paired with a VACUUM method, not a null value or numerical zero.
field_and_context_status.cell_context: No primitive or conventional cell context was returned. These are molecular records, so no periodic-cell normalization or cell equivalence is asserted.
field_and_context_status.explicit_source_nulls: None shown in the returned maps.
field_and_context_status.unavailable_fields: Underlying scientific quantities and calculation lineage were not returned; this is not evidence that their underlying database fields are explicitly null.

mismatches_and_ambiguities: Vibration uses def2-SVPD, whereas both thermo and orbital records use def2-TZVPPD. The NONE records share wB97M-V and VACUUM but do not match the complete level of theory.
No SOLVENT=WATER vibration entry was returned. Its omission does not establish that such a calculation does not exist elsewhere.
All five group-specific property IDs are distinct. None explicitly identifies a shared underlying calculation across groups, and distinct property IDs alone also do not rule out shared source tasks.

No source task IDs, geometry identifiers, or dependency records were returned. In particular, a mixed-level workflow linking vibration corrections to thermo cannot be confirmed or excluded from these maps.
The summary property ID identifies the summary record; it is not an interchangeable thermo, vibration, or orbital endpoint ID.

numerical_audit.status: Unavailable, not zero: the observations contain identifiers and method labels, but no electronic energies, thermal enthalpy corrections, entropies, free energies, frequencies, or orbital energies.

tolerance_policy.displayed_values: Allow one half-unit of the last printed digit per source when propagating rounding uncertainty.

numerical_audit.tolerance_result: Not evaluated: there are no observed numerical operands. The supplied temperature, conversion factor, units, and schema URL do not supply measured calculation values.

results.decision: Retain all five group-specific records separately. Link each ID to its own method using the observed source labels, and annotate the two thermo–orbital method/environment matches. Do not merge outputs as one calculation or derive numerical consistency residuals without underlying values and explicit calculation lineage.
limitations: The supplied tools retrieve summary metadata only; no available tool retrieves the underlying property documents or calculation dependencies.
Successful calls establish that the displayed metadata was returned, not that every scientific field exists or is populated.

Matching molecule identity identifies a common molecular object, not a common electronic-structure calculation. The observed basis-set and solvent differences already require separate provenance; matching full method labels still does not identify a particular source task.

tolerances.rounding_policy: Each component is reported to 0.001 kcal/mol, allowing ±0.0005 kcal/mol per component. The sum therefore allows ±0.0015 kcal/mol worst-case rounding uncertainty; the translational-minus-rotational difference allows ±0.001 kcal/mol. Arithmetic uses the observed numerical values without intermediate rounding; fraction percentages are rounded only for presentation.

results.decision: The three available components have matching source hashes, formula, temperature and units. Their reported sum is 85.646 kilocalorie / mole. Translation and rotation are equal at reported precision; vibration contributes approximately 97.924% and dominates. Conversion and reported equality residuals are zero within the specified tolerances.
limitations: This is component accounting for the supplied completed Q-Chem calculation, not an MP lookup, new calculation, or assignment to an archived molecule ID.

The sum is not an absolute electronic-plus-thermal enthalpy: no electronic energy or independently reported total enthalpy was returned, so a residual against an absolute or total enthalpy is unavailable, not zero.
Separate pV/RT terms may be omitted from these reported components. Their presence, absence or magnitude cannot be established from these observations; no additional term has been assumed or added.

Method, solvent label and primitive/conventional cell context were not returned. Their null entries denote unavailable metadata, not zero values or evidence of a particular method, solvent, or cell convention.
Successful calls established the presence of these three properties only. Unprinted source precision, vibrational zero-point accounting and other scientific fields remain unverified.

limitations: This is a sum of the three reported components, not an absolute electronic-plus-thermal enthalpy. Electronic energy is not supplied by these observations, and separate pV/RT terms may be omitted; no additional term has been assumed or added.

The native enthalpy ratio is exactly 1 for the displayed data. This supports component consistency, not identification of those entries with total molar enthalpy or total Gibbs energy.

analysis.component_convention: The observed native Q-Chem enthalpy entries are equal, giving a component ratio of 1. These are component contributions, not independently established total molar enthalpies. In particular, one should not silently replace the translational entry with a total ideal-gas enthalpy contribution including a pV term and then require a different ratio. The returned evidence does not expose the total-energy/pV bookkeeping needed to audit that convention independently. Likewise, the calculated H−TS values are component combinations, not the molecule's total Gibbs energy.

display_rounding.qualification: Calculations retain the converted values, but the source components are printed to three decimal places; extra derived digits do not imply additional measurement precision. Temperature is shared between components.
display_rounding.temperature_rounding_note: If 298.15 K is also treated as a rounded display rather than an exact calculation setting, its half-digit uncertainty is 0.005 K. Including this and the entropy-temperature cross term gives bounds of approximately 0.00343974 kJ/mol for the translational result and 0.00296362 kJ/mol for the rotational result.

expected_answer.conclusion: The supplied Q-Chem components are internally consistent in provenance, temperature and units. Their enthalpy ratio is exactly 1 at reported precision; Htrans−T Strans is −11.1371784 kcal/mol and Hrot−T Srot is −7.8521617 kcal/mol. Preserve the native component convention rather than silently treating translational_enthalpy as the total ideal-gas translational molar enthalpy.

analysis.native_component_convention: The native fields named translational_enthalpy and rotational_enthalpy are equal in this output. This is consistent with a component convention using 3RT/2 for translation and nonlinear rotation, rather than assigning the ideal-gas pV contribution to translation. Under a total-molar-enthalpy allocation, translation would instead contribute 5RT/2 and nonlinear rotation 3RT/2, giving a ratio of 5/3. That conditional convention is clearly different from the observed ratio of 1. The computed H−TS values therefore retain the native component labels; they are not independently established total molar Gibbs energies.

Even allowing displayed-value rounding, the observed ratio is incompatible with the conditional total-enthalpy ratio of 5/3.

expected_answer.conclusion: The four thermal components belong to the same supplied Q-Chem calculation at 298.15 K. Their SI component combinations are H_trans−T*S_trans = −45265.6675728 J/mol and H_rot−T*S_rot = −28033.2606584 J/mol. The native enthalpy ratio is 1 with zero equality residual, consistent with equal energy-like thermal components rather than a silently imposed total-enthalpy ratio of 5/3. Display rounding and missing convention/standard-state metadata limit stronger thermodynamic claims.

analysis.native_convention: The equal printed translational and rotational contributions are consistent with Q-Chem's energy-like thermal component convention: translation and nonlinear rotation each contribute 3/2 RT. Do not silently reinterpret the translational entry as the complete ideal-gas molar enthalpy contribution 5/2 RT, which additionally assigns the pV term RT to translation. The 5/3 ratio is therefore a different partition convention, not a required equality for these native entries. The computed H-T*S quantities use the fields as returned; they are component combinations, not a verified total molecular Gibbs energy.

IR arrays align by length; all flags are true, including the mode with reported zero intensity. displacement_norms.definition: Euclidean/Frobenius norm of each returned 8-by-3 displacement array, sqrt(sum of its 24 squared components).
displacement_norms.physical_interpretation: These are normalization-dependent vector norms, not measured vibration amplitudes, lengths, thermal excursions or evidence of oscillation strength.
displacement_norms.rounding_and_tolerance: Arithmetic uses the actual returned components without intermediate rounding. With rtol=1e-6 and atol=1e-8, none of these norms equals 1 within the combined tolerance of 1.01e-6. However, allowing 0.0005 per component for the source's three-decimal displacement printing gives a conservative norm uncertainty bound sqrt(24)*0.0005 = approximately 0.00244949 per mode. Every norm is compatible with unity under that rounding allowance. The six-decimal norm display adds at most 0.0000005 of reporting uncertainty.

ir.interpretation: Mode 7 has a returned intensity of 0.0 and a true IR flag. This is a reported numerical zero, not a null or unavailable value. A displayed zero does not establish an exactly zero unrounded intensity or justify changing the supplied activity flag.

Molecular identity indicators were preserved, and the original SMILES was recovered exactly. Default adapter parsing normalized the hydrogen-expanded input to nine feature rows, but changed row order and hydrogen-sensitive feature values; identical molecular identity does not imply identical ordered atom features.

atom_features.details: The expanded input produces only Atom0–Atom8, not separate hydrogen feature rows. Its ordered feature matrix differs from the source. This is not solely a row permutation: for example, the alcohol-bearing carbon is Atom1 in both inputs, but its returned feature vectors differ by 0.0/1.0 entries. Complete original ordered encodings are retained in o004 and o008.

numeric_comparison.assessment: Heavy-atom counts agree exactly. Observed 0.0 versus 1.0 feature differences exceed these tolerances at the displayed precision. Formula, SMILES and InChI comparisons are exact string comparisons.

analysis.parser_convention: The supplied adapters re-create molecules with Chem.MolFromSmiles using default parsing, rather than passing the in-memory AddHs graph between tools. Here, ordinary explicit [H] atoms are normalized out of the parsed atom list, with hydrogen information retained on their heavy-atom neighbors. Consequently, the expanded SMILES contains ten [H] tokens, but its feature call returns nine heavy-atom rows. Explicit-versus-implicit hydrogen bookkeeping can still affect atom features. RemoveHydrogens also parses before calling Chem.RemoveHs, then serializes the recovered molecule.
analysis.recovered_measurement_basis: o005 returned a SMILES exactly identical to the source. Source measurements were therefore reused for the recovered form; identical measurements were not repeated.

results.decision: The round trip exactly recovers the source SMILES and preserves formula, heavy-atom count and standard InChI. Ordered atom-feature equality does not hold between the source and re-parsed hydrogen-expanded form.
limitations: These results describe adapter re-parsing, not features of a hydrogen-retaining in-memory graph; no such feature measurement is available.

decision.basis: The actual Murcko output retains the source's sole six-membered aromatic ring system and removes only the three non-ring heavy atoms of the OCC side chain. Both source and scaffold have one ring and one ring system.

limitations: These are ordinary small-organic graph computations, not evidence that the scaffold is an energetically stable isolated experimental structure; no biological or experimental validity claim is made.

The ring-system tool does not merge spiro-only connections; this does not affect the single-ring input.

expected_answer.conclusion: Labeling the first carbon as 13C preserves the returned elemental formula and the three-heavy-atom count, while increasing average molar mass by 0.99 g/mol at observed precision and isotope-specific exact mass by 1.003354840 Da. The shifts differ because the two conventions use different reference masses for unlabeled carbon.

analysis.explanation: The average-molar-mass tool uses average atomic weights for unlabeled atoms and respects explicit isotope labels. The exact-mass tool uses isotope-specific masses, with the usual monoisotopic assignments for unlabeled atoms. Thus replacement of the first unlabeled carbon by 13C is measured against different carbon reference masses under the two conventions. Average molar mass is reported in g/mol; exact molecular mass is reported here in Da per molecule. Their numerical values need not agree.

isotope_labeled_counterpart.isotope_label: 13C on the first carbon, explicitly [13CH3]; supplied atom order preserved.

decision.formula_and_heavy_atom_count: Both returned formulas are C2H6O and both heavy-atom counts are 3; these outputs are unchanged.
decision.mass_comparison: Both masses increase upon the supplied isotope substitution. The average and exact numerical values, and their shifts, do not agree within rtol=1e-6 and atol=1e-8, even allowing for the displayed average-mass precision.

limitations: The returned formula omits isotope annotation; C2H6O alone does not establish isotope identity. The original [13CH3]CO identifier retains the actual label.
Average molar masses are available only to 0.01 g/mol. The 0.99 g/mol shift is a subtraction of rounded observations, not an unrounded measurement.
The exact-mass output does not print a unit; Da is the unit interpretation of the RDKit CalcExactMolWt result.
All eight requested measurements returned complete outputs. No fingerprints or other encodings were requested or obtained; no fingerprint equality or on-bit count is established.
These are ordinary small-organic graph computations, not experimental validation or biological-property claims.

expected_answer.conclusion: Labeling the first methyl carbon as 13C leaves the returned elemental formula and four-heavy-atom count unchanged, while increasing the observed average molar mass by 0.99 g/mol and the isotope-specific exact mass by 1.003354840 Da. The different shifts reflect different mass conventions, not inconsistent isotope labeling.

analysis.explanation: The average-mass tool uses average atomic weights for unlabeled atoms and respects explicit isotope labels. The exact-mass tool uses monoisotopic masses for unlabeled atoms and the specified isotope mass for labeled atoms. Consequently, replacing an average-weight carbon with 13C differs from replacing 12C with 13C; both absolute masses and isotope shifts need not agree. Exact mass in Da per molecule is numerically comparable to its corresponding molar mass in g/mol, but the conventions differ.

average_molar_mass.precision: Calculated from the returned two-decimal masses only.

decision.isotope_identity: The shared returned formula does not establish isotope identity; retain the distinct supplied SMILES unchanged.
decision.mass_comparison: Both average and exact masses increase upon labeling. Neither the absolute masses nor their shifts agree numerically across conventions at rtol=1e-6 and atol=1e-8, even allowing for the displayed average-mass precision.

limitations: The formula tool returned C3H6O for both inputs and did not encode the explicit 13C label. The isotope label is preserved in the supplied SMILES, not in that formula output.
Average molar masses are available only to two decimal places; no hidden precision is inferred for their shift.
The exact-mass output has no printed unit; Da is the unit interpretation of the contracted RDKit CalcExactMolWt calculation.
No fingerprints or additional identifier encodings were obtained; fingerprint equality and on-bit counts are unavailable.
These are ordinary small-organic graph calculations, not experimental measurements or biological-validity claims.

analysis.explanation: Average molar mass uses RDKit average atomic weights for unlabeled atoms while respecting explicit isotope labels. Exact mass uses isotope-specific masses for labeled atoms and monoisotopic masses for unlabeled atoms. Consequently, replacing the first unlabeled carbon with carbon-13 produces different shifts under the two conventions. Da denotes mass per molecule; g/mol denotes molar mass. The exact-mass tool does not print a unit; Da is the conventional interpretation of its CalcExactMolWt result.

expected_answer.conclusion: For these two supplied SMILES, standard InChI verifies the same encoded molecular identity, including stereochemistry. Morgan encoding is unchanged, and both invariant arrays agree exactly once atom order is mapped. This is evidence of reordering invariance for this pair, not proof that hashed fingerprints uniquely identify molecules.

Morgan_fingerprint.comparison: Exact equality of complete returned on-bit lists.

atom_reordering.indexing: Zero-based atom indices in each supplied SMILES parsing order.

analysis.comparison_policy: Identifiers, bit indices and integer invariants were compared exactly. All numeric results are dimensionless. Exact mapped equality also satisfies rtol=1e-6 and atol=1e-8; no rounding was applied.

results.decision: The supplied encodings have identical standard InChI, equal Morgan fingerprints with 11 on-bits each, and exactly equal connectivity and feature invariants after accounting for atom-index reordering.
limitations: All returned on-bit lists and invariant arrays are complete; no truncated or unavailable encoding was used to establish equality or counts. A dense fingerprint vector was not requested.

Hashed fingerprint equality alone is not proof of molecular identity: distinct graphs can collide. No distinct-graph collision is demonstrated here; identity is independently supported by the identical stereochemical standard InChI.
The supplied Morgan implementation uses radius 2 and does not explicitly enable chirality-sensitive fingerprinting. Its equality should not be treated as independent verification of stereochemistry.
Connectivity and feature invariants are atom-level encodings, not standalone proofs of graph identity.
Results concern only these ordinary small-organic graph computations; they make no biological-property or experimental-validity claim.

portable_export.scope: Selected necessary successful real tool results; not a complete model conversation.

question: Morgan encoding invariance under SMILES reordering. Use the supplied alternative SMILES encodings of the same intended graph. First verify identity by actual standard InChI, then compare Morgan fingerprints and connectivity/feature invariants with atom-index reordering accounted for. Report equal/unequal fingerprints, on-bit counts where applicable and distinguish a hashed collision from a proof of identity. Use only the supplied ordinary small-molecule inputs and actual observations. Preserve atom order, units and exact identifiers. Numeric comparisons use rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-8, with displayed precision respected. Report truncated or unavailable encodings explicitly; only complete returned data can establish exact fingerprint equality or on-bit counts. Report a concise evidence-backed conclusion and limitations.

required_outputs.analysis: Actual requested representations, identifiers, graph/feature results and exact object/index alignment.
required_outputs.decision: The requested scientific consistency comparison supported by actual observations.
required_outputs.limitations: Output precision, encoding conventions and stated limits; no biological/experimental claim.

assistant_review_records.notes: Direct Codex source/family review and per-record critical-conclusion/evidence-packet review, supported by exact journal alignment and independent numeric definitions. Checked object/row identity, native units, uncertainty/rounding, training-only preprocessing, actual artifacts, required outputs, and meaningful step removal. This is assistant review, not human expert review; supplemental RDKit/SciPy backend checks are labeled and are not claimed as fully independent algorithms. All raw actor outputs/attempts remain unchanged. Selected reference steps omit duplicate, superseded and arithmetic-only scaffolding; independent branches aggregate at final_answer without invented serial dependencies. Reviewed morgan_invariance in the declared scientific scope. Nulls/truncated data remain explicit; conditional or negative findings do not become unqualified scientific success claims.

remediation.archival_evidence_recovery: per-output SHA256 checked; no scientific tool re-execution implied

algorithm_check.assessment: The fingerprint family and radius match. The matrix describes its metric as Tanimoto, consistent with the default similarity operation. No backend mismatch is evident in the returned values.
algorithm_check.distance_tool: The supplied implementation uses Morgan bit-vector fingerprints with radius=2 and distance = 1 − DataStructs.FingerprintSimilarity. Bit length and similarity metric are implicit defaults.
algorithm_check.similarity_tool: The supplied implementation uses Morgan bit-vector fingerprints with radius=2, nBits=2048, and explicit DataStructs.TanimotoSimilarity.

invariants.diagonal: Diagonal entries are '-', not measured numeric zeros. Self-distance 0 and self-similarity 1 are mathematical expectations, not returned diagonal observations.
invariants.pair_ordering: The molecule list uses zero-based Mol 0–2, but table headers use one-based Mol 1–3. Mapping by panel position gives the pairs (0,1), (0,2), (1,2). For this three-molecule panel, the supplied packed-distance construction and upper-triangle rendering preserve that ordering.
invariants.symmetry: Only the upper triangle is returned. Tanimoto distance is symmetric by the implemented definition, but reverse-direction entries were not observed; the displayed table cannot independently verify symmetry.

analysis.numeric_test: Using rtol=1e-6 and atol=1e-8, all three displayed distances equal 1 minus the displayed similarities. Distances are printed to four decimal places; similarity values are rounded to four decimal places, with trailing zeros omitted.
analysis.units: Dimensionless distances and similarities; input SMILES and atom order were unchanged.

results.decision: All three unordered pairs show displayed-precision complement agreement. This is not proof of unrounded agreement or exact runtime fingerprint-parameter identity.
limitations: No complete fingerprint encodings were requested or returned. Exact fingerprint equality and on-bit counts therefore cannot be established; no encoding truncation was observed because no encodings were supplied.
Rounded outputs cannot establish the stated tight tolerance for the underlying unrounded values.
Symmetry and diagonal values are definition-based expectations rather than fully populated matrix observations.
The findings concern ordinary small-organic graph computation only, not biological properties or experimental validity.

expected_answer.conclusion: All three returned unordered pairs satisfy distance = 1 − similarity at displayed precision. The supplied implementations use compatible Morgan-radius-2/Tanimoto methods, subject to the distance tool's unexposed default fingerprint length. Pair ordering is correct for this panel despite inconsistent zero-based versus one-based labels. The triangular output does not directly verify symmetry or diagonal values, and no fingerprint encodings were available.

algorithm_check.compatibility: These use the same fingerprint family, radius and similarity metric. The distance implementation relies on the usual 2048-bit default rather than explicitly specifying it. The returned observations do not independently expose the runtime default. No different-fingerprint backend mismatch is evidenced.
algorithm_check.distance: The supplied implementation uses RDKit Morgan bit-vector fingerprints with radius=2 and FingerprintSimilarity (default Tanimoto), then computes 1 minus similarity. Fingerprint length is left at the RDKit default.
algorithm_check.similarity: The supplied implementation uses RDKit Morgan bit-vector fingerprints with radius=2, explicitly nBits=2048, and TanimotoSimilarity.

matrix_invariants.diagonal: Self-distance is mathematically 0 and self-similarity 1 for these fingerprints. The returned diagonal contains '-', so numeric diagonal values were not observed.
matrix_invariants.pair_ordering: The identifier list uses Mol 0–2, while table labels use Mol 1–3. Both follow input order. For this three-molecule panel, packed computation order (second, first), (third, first), (third, second) maps correctly to displayed upper-triangle pairs (first, second), (first, third), (second, third).
matrix_invariants.symmetry: Expected from the symmetric Tanimoto metric. Only the upper triangle was returned; lower-triangle entries are '-' rather than independently measured values.

decision.backend_mismatch: None observed; fingerprint-length compatibility depends on the distance backend's default.
decision.distance_equals_one_minus_similarity: All three pairs pass comparison of the returned displayed values using rtol=1e-6 and atol=1e-8. This establishes displayed-value consistency, not full-precision equality.

limitations: Distances are displayed to four decimal places; similarities are rounded to four decimal places, with trailing zeros omitted. Differences below the reporting resolution cannot be assessed at the requested numerical tolerances.

No fingerprint encodings were returned by these measurements. Exact fingerprint equality, encoding completeness and on-bit counts are unavailable; they cannot be inferred from these similarity scores.
Input SMILES and their order were preserved without canonicalization or identifier substitution.
Symmetry and diagonal values are implementation-level expectations, not independently returned numeric measurements.
The observations concern ordinary small-organic graph computation only; they establish no biological property or experimental validity.

expected_answer.conclusion: For CC(=O)CC(=O)C, seven consistently indexed atoms produce four local atom-code environments and 21 unordered graph pairs. Actual pair-score explanations confirm endpoint-environment and one-bond separation information. The truncated fingerprint prevents exact fingerprint equality, on-bit counts or fingerprint count-sum validation.

atom_features.checks: Inspection recovered all seven feature rows from the truncated preview. Rows 0 and 6, 1 and 4, and 2 and 5 are respectively identical; row 3 is distinct. These groups agree with the per-atom code groups. Feature-column names were not returned, so individual vector positions are not assigned chemical meanings.

analysis.comparison_policy: rtol=1e-6 and atol=1e-8, respecting displayed precision. The reported code identities, feature-row matches and integer-valued distance checks agree exactly; no hidden fingerprint entries were compared.

count_consistency.interpretation: Seven atoms yield 7×6/2 = 21 unordered distinct-atom pairs, matching the matrix histogram. This is a graph-pair count, not an observed fingerprint count sum or on-bit count.

distance_matrix.checks: The complete 7×7 matrix is symmetric with zero diagonal. Distance-one pairs are (0,1), (1,2), (1,3), (3,4), (4,5), (4,6). The carbonyl double bond (1,2) still has topological distance 1.
distance_matrix.units: Number of bonds along the shortest graph path; not a spatial distance.

analysis.explanation_provenance: Actual ExplainAtomCode outputs for indices 0–3 reproduce the four distinct GetAtomPairCode identifiers exactly. The returned per-atom codes describe local environments, not pair separations.

fingerprint.status: Obtained, but encoding is internally truncated by the tool's array formatting.

analysis.indexing: Zero-based source atom order is preserved: 0 C, 1 C, 2 O, 3 C, 4 C, 5 O, 6 C. No explicit hydrogen rows are returned.
analysis.pair_score_interpretation: Both actual pair-score explanations encode endpoint environments and separation, and their distance 1 agrees with the matrix. Only confirmed adjacent pairs were submitted: this tool's implementation fixes dist=1, so it cannot validate arbitrary nonadjacent separations.

results.decision: Atom indexing, local-environment grouping and graph-distance counts are consistent across the complete returned data. Fingerprint-level equality and count consistency remain unverified.
limitations: The fingerprint's ellipsis is in the returned string itself; a complete stored string is not a complete numeric encoding. Displayed zeros do not imply an empty fingerprint.
Per-atom codes, explained pair scores and fingerprint coordinates are not treated as interchangeable hash spaces. No fingerprint coordinate is decoded from these pair-score examples.
Feature vectors were recovered completely, but their column schema was not supplied.
All findings concern the supplied ordinary small-organic graph only; they establish no biological property or experimental validity.

expected_answer.conclusion: The same ordered six-atom source yields six feature rows, six local-code rows and a consistent 6-by-6 bond-distance matrix containing 15 unordered atom pairs. Actual explanations demonstrate local environment encoding and a chirality-dependent code difference. Fingerprint truncation prevents exact fingerprint or nonzero-count claims; distinct encoding spaces were not conflated.

atom_features.note: The initially abbreviated preview was recovered by inspection. Feature vectors have no returned column labels; no unsupported column-by-column decoding is assigned. Rows 2 and 5 are identical.

analysis.atom_indexing: Zero-based, in source SMILES order; hydrogens are not separate indexed atoms. All four descriptor outputs identify the same source.

code_interpretation.chirality: For atom 1, ExplainAtomCode with chirality enabled returns 1059 and S; with chirality disabled it returns 35, matching GetAtomPairCode. Thus the returned per-atom code 35 does not retain that chirality distinction.
code_interpretation.encoding_space_caution: The observed pair-score decoder combines two local environments and separation. Per-atom codes, pair scores and fingerprint coordinates are distinct representations; no fingerprint coordinate is decoded by assuming it shares the pair-score encoding.
code_interpretation.nonuniqueness: Atoms 2 and 5 both have code 97 despite different positions and functional-group contexts; these local codes are not unique atom identifiers.
code_interpretation.observed_environments: Explanations give (element, neighbor count after branchSubtract, pi-electron count): 33 = (C,1,0); 35 = (C,3,0); 97 = (O,1,0); 43 = (C,3,1); 105 = (O,1,1).

count_consistency.finding: Atom-level counts and graph-pair counts agree. Fifteen graph pairs do not imply fifteen distinct fingerprint coordinates.

fingerprint.note: Displayed zeros do not establish an all-zero fingerprint. Its full length, nonzero coordinates and count sum are unavailable.
fingerprint.status: Internally truncated by the tool's array formatting.

numeric_comparison.finding: Complete displayed integer codes and graph distances agree exactly where compared, hence within the requested tolerances. No comparison is made against omitted fingerprint entries.

topological_distance.checks: Symmetric 6-by-6 matrix with zero diagonal. Distance-one pairs are (0,1), (1,2), (1,3), (3,4), (3,5), matching the source connectivity. The double bond (3,4) has topological distance 1.
topological_distance.units: Number of bonds traversed, not angstroms or bond-order sums.

results.decision: Atom indexing, local-code explanations and topological separation are supported and count-consistent. Exact fingerprint equality, on-bit/nonzero counts and fingerprint multiplicity consistency remain unestablished.
limitations: The fingerprint tool returned an ellipsis-containing string; inspecting that string cannot recover omitted entries.
Atom-feature column semantics are not supplied by the output.
Pair-score examples cover directly connected pairs only; the supplied explanation tool fixes distance to 1. Longer separations are supported by the distance matrix, not by additional decoded scores.
No alternative molecule or fingerprint was supplied for an equality comparison.
These are ordinary small-organic graph computations, not biological-property predictions or experimental validation.

expected_answer.conclusion: The torsion encoding separates these inputs completely at the feature-identifier level, whereas the atom-pair encoding retains one shared feature at different counts. The analogue has one ring versus none in the source, but equal rotatable-bond counts. The two encodings capture complementary graph information and should not be directly mixed for similarity calculations.

encoding_comparison.atom_pairs: Atom-pair features encode atom types together with graph separations, rather than only four-atom paths. The fingerprints share exactly one identifier, 705601, with source count 2 and analogue count 1; all other returned identifiers differ.
encoding_comparison.numeric_comparison: Counts are returned as exact integers. Equality and difference statements are unchanged under rtol=1e-6 and atol=1e-8. Identifiers are compared exactly, not approximately.
encoding_comparison.torsions: Topological torsions encode four-atom path environments. The two complete torsion fingerprints share no encoded identifiers.

analysis.representation: Complete sparse integer count fingerprints: encoded feature identifier → occurrence count. These are not fixed-length binary bit vectors; nonzero-entry counts below are not binary on-bit counts. All counts are dimensionless.

results.decision: Neither fingerprint is exactly equal between the molecules. The analogue has more distinct features and total occurrences under both conventions, while both molecules have 2 rotatable bonds. No similarity score was computed; comparisons were made within each matching fingerprint convention, not between torsion and atom-pair identifier spaces.
limitations: No encoding was truncated or unavailable in the returned sparse listings; these complete listings support the reported equality and nonzero-entry conclusions.
Input SMILES and their atom order were preserved without rewriting. Feature identifiers are encoded labels, not atom indices or physical measurements.
Topological torsions describe graph paths, not measured dihedral angles or conformational populations; atom-pair separations are graph distances, not spatial distances.
Results are limited to ordinary small-organic graph computation. They establish no biological property, experimental validity, or general analogue similarity.

expected_answer.conclusion: The analogue has one additional ring and one additional rotatable bond, plus more distinct and repeated features under both fingerprint conventions. Torsions describe four-atom environments; atom-pairs additionally characterize graph separations. Complete returned count encodings establish that the molecules differ under both conventions.

observed_differences.interpretation: Topological torsions encode connected four-atom environments, not measured dihedral angles. Atom-pairs encode atom-type pairs together with graph separations, not spatial distances. Both conventions show repeated encodings in the analogue, whereas every returned source feature has count 1. Feature identifiers from the two fingerprint families are different encoding spaces and should not be compared across families.

analysis.representation: Complete sparse, unfolded integer count fingerprints: each exact feature identifier maps to its occurrence count. These are not binary bit vectors; nonzero-feature counts are reported, not on-bit counts.
analysis.units_and_comparison: Feature occurrences, rings and bonds are dimensionless integer counts. Graph separations refer to bond-path lengths. SMILES and exact feature identifiers are preserved. Integer comparisons are exact and satisfy rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-8 without rounding.

results.decision: The source and analogue fingerprints are unequal within each matched convention, with disjoint nonzero identifier sets in both families. No cross-family similarity or numerical similarity score was computed.
limitations: All four returned fingerprint listings are complete; no truncated encoding was used. Dense or folded binary encodings and their on-bit counts were not returned.
These observations do not establish stereochemical discrimination: retaining @ in the input does not demonstrate that the fingerprint encodes chirality.
Rotatable-bond counts follow the supplied tool's RDKit definition. This is ordinary small-organic graph computation only, with no biological-property or experimental-validity claim.

No unmatched or multiply typed atoms are observed.

analysis.index_interpretation: Atom indices are the one-based displayed molecular atom order. Fingerprint indices 7, 9 and 34 are atom-type group identifiers, not molecular atom indices. precision_and_agreement.units: EState indices and their sums are dimensionless descriptor values; counts are numbers of atoms.

limitations: The observations provide formatted outputs, not full-precision numerical arrays. This verifies conservation at the available precision, not bitwise equality of underlying values.
All displayed atom entries and nonzero fingerprint groups are present, with no visible truncation. Zero-count fingerprint bins are intentionally omitted by the tool.
The fingerprint's type-name mapping is inferred from matching counts and sums rather than independently verified against a supplied group-index dictionary.

question: BCUT molecular-cohort projection and clustering. Compute all eight native BCUT2D coordinates for each supplied molecule in the declared order. Fit per-column population standardization on this descriptive cohort, retaining constant columns with scale one, then project to two principal components and cluster those actual scores into two k-means groups with seed 42. Report means/scales, retained variance, scores, memberships and centroids. Component signs/cluster labels are arbitrary, and four molecules cannot support a physical-property or generalization claim. Use actual successful observations, preserve artifact identity and hashes, and report native units/precision. Numerical agreement uses rtol=1e-6 and atol=1e-8 with propagated printed-digit uncertainty; missing or truncated outputs cannot be silently filled. Give an evidence-backed conclusion and limitations.

workflow_goal: BCUT molecular-cohort projection and clustering: Compute all eight native BCUT2D coordinates for each supplied molecule in the declared order. Fit per-column population standardization on this descriptive cohort, retaining constant columns with scale one, then project to two principal components and cluster those actual scores into two k-means groups with seed 42. Report means/scales, retained variance, scores, memberships and centroids. Component signs/cluster labels are arbitrary, and four molecules cannot support a physical-property or generalization claim.

expected_answer.conclusion: Successful observations establish a complete, identity-preserved BCUT → population-standardization → two-PC → k-means workflow. The projection retains about 89.51% of cohort variance and separates benzene from the other three molecules in this specific two-group solution. This is a descriptive geometric result only, not a physical-property or generalization claim.

PCA.method: Full-SVD PCA fitted to the same standardized cohort, retaining two components; no additional scaling.

clustering.method: Euclidean k-means on the actual two-component scores; k=2, seed=42, n_init=10.

precision_policy.handling: No intermediate rounding; native markdown values were transferred with every available digit, then numeric arrays were transferred by observation binding. Printed-digit uncertainty remains inherited. All required outputs were available; no missing values were filled.

standardization.method: Per-column cohort mean and population standard deviation (ddof=0); transform (x-mean)/scale. Constant columns are retained with scale one.

analysis.units_and_precision: Values are native RDKit BCUT2D matrix eigenvalues, with mass, Gasteiger-charge, Crippen-logP and Crippen-MR atom weighting respectively. They are descriptor coordinates, not measured molecular mass, net charge, logP or molar refractivity. The tool supplies no explicit eigenvalue unit metadata. All available printed digits are preserved; no experimental accuracy is implied. Standardized coordinates, PCA scores and centroids are dimensionless numerical coordinates.

results.decision: The descriptive two-PC projection retains 89.51481056469898% of standardized cohort variance. In the observed seed-42 k-means result, M2 (benzene) forms a singleton group and M0, M1 and M3 form the other group.
limitations: Only four molecules were analyzed, with all preprocessing fitted on that same descriptive cohort; there is no held-out evaluation or generalization evidence.
No biological endpoint, experimental property or reaction outcome was supplied. Clusters do not establish physical-property classes or biological activity.
The two-component projection discards approximately 10.4852% of standardized variance; clustering describes this projection rather than the complete eight-coordinate space.
Component signs and cluster labels are arbitrary. Membership depends on the chosen descriptor representation, cohort scaling, projection and clustering settings; stability was not tested.
Native BCUT coordinates are computed eigenvalue descriptors rather than experimental measurements. Software-version metadata and output hashes were not supplied.

question: BCUT molecular-cohort projection and clustering. Compute all eight native BCUT2D coordinates for each supplied molecule in the declared order. Fit per-column population standardization on this descriptive cohort, retaining constant columns with scale one, then project to two principal components and cluster those actual scores into two k-means groups with seed 42. Report means/scales, retained variance, scores, memberships and centroids. Component signs/cluster labels are arbitrary, and four molecules cannot support a physical-property or generalization claim. Use actual successful observations, preserve artifact identity and hashes, and report native units/precision. Numerical agreement uses rtol=1e-6 and atol=1e-8 with propagated printed-digit uncertainty; missing or truncated outputs cannot be silently filled. Give an evidence-backed conclusion and limitations.

required_outputs.decision: The scientific comparison and supported conclusion requested above; explicit unavailable fields.
required_outputs.limitations: Assumptions, artifact/descriptor conventions and scientific scope; no invented measurement.

workflow_goal: BCUT molecular-cohort projection and clustering: Compute all eight native BCUT2D coordinates for each supplied molecule in the declared order. Fit per-column population standardization on this descriptive cohort, retaining constant columns with scale one, then project to two principal components and cluster those actual scores into two k-means groups with seed 42. Report means/scales, retained variance, scores, memberships and centroids. Component signs/cluster labels are arbitrary, and four molecules cannot support a physical-property or generalization claim.

expected_answer.conclusion: Successful observations support a reproducible descriptive two-PC projection and two-group partition of this cohort: {M1, M2} and {M0, M3}. The projection retains about 92.62% of standardized variance, but neither the clusters nor the projection justify physical-property or generalization claims.

kmeans.method: Euclidean k-means on the actual two-dimensional PCA scores, two clusters, ten initializations, seed 42.

pca.method: Two-component PCA fitted to the exact standardized cohort artifact; the same cohort was projected.
pca.variance_convention: PCA explained variances use the sample covariance convention; input standardization uses population scales.

provenance.completeness: All successful numerical outputs used here were complete. Truncated argument previews were not used to reconstruct arrays; exact stored artifacts were transferred by observation binding. An unrelated invalid standardization call, o008, failed and contributed no result.
provenance.hash_scope: These are the executor-supplied argument hashes, not output hashes. No other hashes were supplied or invented.
provenance.identity: PCA inputs were bound directly to o005.features; k-means inputs were bound directly to o006.features. Native markdown coordinates were transcribed without rounding for standardization.

standardization.method: Per-column cohort mean and population standard deviation, using all four rows as both fitting and transformation data. All eight columns were retained; none is constant. The tool uses scale one for constant columns.

analysis.units_and_precision: Native, unconverted BCUT2D descriptor eigenvalues are reported with every digit printed by GetBCUT. The tool identifies mass-, Gasteiger-charge-, Crippen-logP- and Crippen-MR-weighted coordinates but supplies no formal eigenvalue unit metadata; these are not direct measurements of molecular mass, charge, logP or molar refractivity. Standardized coordinates and PCA scores are dimensionless. No precision beyond the observed printed digits is claimed.

results.decision: The requested descriptive pipeline succeeded. Two PCs retain approximately 92.6175% of standardized cohort variance. K-means groups M1 with M2 and M0 with M3 in that observed score space.
limitations: Only four molecules were analyzed, with no endpoint, experimental property, reaction outcome, external validation set or golden answer.
This cohort-fitted standardization and PCA describe these four molecules only; they do not demonstrate predictive performance or generalization.

Cluster membership describes similarity under the chosen descriptors, scaling, two-PC projection and Euclidean k-means objective. It does not establish physical-property classes or biological activity.
Component signs and cluster labels are arbitrary. The two-PC projection discards approximately 7.3825% of standardized variance.

Reported numbers retain observed precision; printed-digit uncertainty must be considered with the requested rtol=1e-6 and atol=1e-8. No independent numerical agreement test or additional uncertainty estimate was performed.

question: BCUT molecular-cohort projection and clustering. Compute all eight native BCUT2D coordinates for each supplied molecule in the declared order. Fit per-column population standardization on this descriptive cohort, retaining constant columns with scale one, then project to two principal components and cluster those actual scores into two k-means groups with seed 42. Report means/scales, retained variance, scores, memberships and centroids. Component signs/cluster labels are arbitrary, and four molecules cannot support a physical-property or generalization claim. Use actual successful observations, preserve artifact identity and hashes, and report native units/precision. Numerical agreement uses rtol=1e-6 and atol=1e-8 with propagated printed-digit uncertainty; missing or truncated outputs cannot be silently filled. Give an evidence-backed conclusion and limitations.

workflow_goal: BCUT molecular-cohort projection and clustering: Compute all eight native BCUT2D coordinates for each supplied molecule in the declared order. Fit per-column population standardization on this descriptive cohort, retaining constant columns with scale one, then project to two principal components and cluster those actual scores into two k-means groups with seed 42. expected_answer.conclusion: All four successful native WHIM outputs were parsed without truncation into a 4×114 matrix. No columns are constant. Cohort population standardization followed by two-component PCA retains 81.69686407864245% of variance; seed-42 two-group k-means yields {M0, M1, M2} and {M3}. This is an evidence-backed computational feature summary, not a measured-geometry result or a validated property classification. Higher-precision native descriptors and stronger conformer provenance would be needed to certify hidden-value numerical agreement and uncertainty-stable memberships.

artifact_identity.hash_scope: Executor-reported argument/output artifact hashes, not hashes of conformer coordinates or independently canonicalized numeric matrices. No hashes were supplied for o001–o004 or o008.
artifact_identity.transfer: The parsed matrix, standardized features and PCA scores were passed downstream through exact successful-observation bindings, not rounded reconstructions. Truncated display previews were not used as substitute arrays.

clustering.method: Euclidean k-means on the exact two-component scores; two clusters, ten initializations, seed 42.

native_features.coordinate_order: Unchanged native CalcWHIM order; no coordinates dropped or imputed.
native_features.precision: Native outputs contain at most three decimal places. Parsing preserves the reported numerical values; subsequent floating-point digits do not recover unreported descriptor precision.
native_features.units: Values are reported unchanged in the tool's native WHIM convention. The supplied outputs do not specify coordinate names, weighting-block definitions or per-coordinate units; assigning a single physical unit to all 114 coordinates would not be justified.

numerical_uncertainty.agreement_status: No independent reference is supplied, so numerical agreement cannot be tested. Results are conditional on the actual printed native vectors.
numerical_uncertainty.conditional_printed_digit_propagation: If the native values were rounded to the nearest 0.001, each coordinate has a maximum rounding error epsilon=0.0005. Cohort means and population scales each then have error at most epsilon. For a reported standardized coordinate z with population scale s, a conservative propagated bound is |delta z| <= epsilon*(2+|z|)/(s-epsilon). This includes refitting the mean and scale, not merely dividing raw rounding error by s.
numerical_uncertainty.implication: Small-scale columns amplify native rounding uncertainty. The minimum scale is about 0.00887; hidden unrounded features cannot be assumed to reproduce these results within the requested floating-point tolerances.
numerical_uncertainty.unresolved: The tool does not certify its rounding rule or expose higher-precision WHIM values. Numerical uncertainty intervals for refitted PCA scores, retained variance and cluster assignments were not established; the reported memberships are not certified invariant to hidden printed-digit uncertainty.

pca.method: Full-SVD PCA fitted to the cohort-standardized matrix; two components.

analysis.protocol: Chem.MolFromSmiles, Chem.AddHs, AllChem.EmbedMolecule(randomSeed=42), then rdMolDescriptors.CalcWHIM. No geometry optimization is shown in the supplied implementation. These are computational conformers, not measured geometries.

standardization.method: Columnwise cohort mean subtraction and population-standard-deviation division, fitted on all four samples.
standardization.verification: Every inspected population scale is positive and none equals the tool's constant-feature replacement scale of 1. The smallest reported scale is 0.008870597499605094.

decision.interpretation: For this four-molecule computational cohort, two PCs retain approximately 81.70% of standardized variance. Seed-42 k-means separates M3 from M0, M1 and M2. Cluster numbers are arbitrary identifiers, not chemical or biological classes.

expected_answer.conclusion: All four successful WHIM outputs contain 114 coordinates, preserved in native order without filling or truncating values. No cohort columns are constant. Population-standardized two-component PCA retains 85.06% of variance, and seed-42 k-means groups {M1, M2} and {M0, M3}. This is an evidence-backed computational description of the returned conformer descriptors, not a measured-geometry result or a predictive biological conclusion; unrounded precision and propagated-uncertainty agreement remain unverified.

artifact_identity.hash_scope: Executor-reported SHA-256 values for stored output artifacts, not hashes of molecular coordinates or individual native WHIM strings.
artifact_identity.transfer: Stored arrays were bound directly from o005 to o006, o006 to o007, and o007 to o008. Truncated display previews were not used as numerical inputs.
artifact_identity.unavailable_hashes: No source-conformer hashes or output hashes for o001–o004 and o008 were supplied; none are invented.

native_features.constant_column_basis: Comparison of the parsed cohort coordinates and inspection of all 114 population scales in o006.
native_features.coordinate_order: Unchanged native CalcWHIM output order; all 114 returned coordinates per molecule were parsed, with no imputation or truncation.
native_features.precision: The returned native numbers have at most three decimal places. Downstream floating-point digits describe calculations on those printed inputs, not additional native descriptor precision.
native_features.units: Native, unconverted CalcWHIM descriptor values. The tool supplies no coordinate names or per-coordinate unit metadata; assigning one physical unit to the entire vector is not supported.

protocol.conformers: The supplied tool parses SMILES, adds explicit hydrogens, calls EmbedMolecule with randomSeed=42, and calls CalcWHIM. Its implementation shows no geometry optimization. These are computational conformers, not measured geometries.
protocol.preprocessing: Population standardization fitted on all four cohort rows; PCA fitted to that same standardized cohort using full SVD, retaining two components; Euclidean k-means on those scores with two clusters, ten initializations and seed 42.

decision.interpretation: Two PCs retain approximately 85.06% of standardized cohort variance. The requested clustering pairs M1 with M2 and M0 with M3; numerical cluster labels are arbitrary.

numerical_agreement.assessment: No independent reference or golden answer was supplied, so agreement at these tolerances cannot be asserted. Exact stored downstream artifacts are retained for comparison.
numerical_agreement.printed_digit_uncertainty: If the native outputs were rounded to the nearest 0.001, each input coordinate would have a rounding uncertainty of up to 0.0005, including printed zeros. The supplied tools do not expose unrounded descriptors or propagate such intervals through standardization, PCA and k-means. A propagated-uncertainty agreement or membership-stability certificate is therefore not claimed.

decision.status: Completed for the complete native vectors actually returned by the supplied tool.

limitations: Only four molecules were used. Cohort centering permits at most three nonzero principal components; this is descriptive compression, not externally validated generalization.

Native printed precision cannot be recovered by reporting more downstream digits. Full internal CalcWHIM precision, coordinate-specific units and toolkit version were not supplied.

expected_answer.conclusion: The observed records consistently identify acetone, CAS 67-64-1, PubChem CID 180, formula C3H6O and InChIKey CSCPPACGZOOCGX-UHFFFAOYSA-N. Database resolution preserves standard InChI identity despite a different SMILES spelling, and the retrieved MOL connectivity agrees. CAS uniqueness beyond these records and experimental 3D geometry are not established.

cas_identity.assessment: Unambiguous within the returned records, but not an exhaustive registry uniqueness determination.
cas_identity.evidence: The name lookup reports CAS 67-64-1 for CID 180. Resolving 67-64-1 independently returns CID 180 and the same canonical SMILES as the acetone-name lookup.
cas_identity.qualification: The CAS tool returns only the first CAS entry of the first matching CID; it does not enumerate all aliases, alternative records or registry assignments.

precision_and_units.identifiers_and_formula: Compared exactly as categorical strings and atom counts; numerical tolerances do not apply.
precision_and_units.mol_coordinates: Coordinate fields are preserved in the referenced artifact at four decimal places. The returned text supplies no explicit coordinate unit. Its 2D coordinates are not interpreted as measured molecular dimensions.
precision_and_units.numerical_agreement: No corresponding numerical measurements were supplied for comparison under rtol=1e-6 and atol=1e-8. If nearest-digit rounding were assumed, four-decimal coordinate fields would carry ±0.00005 printed-digit uncertainty in their unspecified coordinate units; no coordinate agreement test was performed.

round_trip.explanation: Both distinct SMILES strings generate exactly the same standard InChI and formula. All three database reverse lookups used exactly the locally generated InChIKey. Because the returned InChI is identical to the original key-generation input, its deterministic local key is also identical; a redundant key-generation call was not made.
round_trip.mol_assessment: The complete V2000 record is labeled 180 and RDKit 2D. It contains four explicit atoms (three carbon and one oxygen) and three bonds: one C=O double bond and two C–C single bonds, consistent with acetone. Hydrogens are implicit. This is a connection table, not evidence of measured 3D coordinates.

analysis.upstream_status: All requested lookups succeeded. No transient upstream failure was observed.

results.decision: PASS for the observed formula and encoded-identity round trip. Exact standard InChI identity is established, and every reverse-lookup key exactly matches the locally generated key. CAS-to-name structure consistency is supported within PubChem.
limitations: Only the two NameToSMILES responses expose fetch timestamps, response modes and response SHA256 hashes. CAS and key-resolution outputs expose no such metadata; none was inferred.
Reported hashes identify upstream responses, not the normalized SMILES output or the RDKit-rewritten MOL. No separate MOL or output-artifact hash was available.
No MOL-to-InChI conversion tool is supplied. MOL connectivity was checked directly, not independently converted to an InChIKey.
The MOL is RDKit serialization of a retrieved connection table, not an unchanged raw PubChem SDF or proof of experimental geometry.
No experimental property, biological endpoint, reaction result or reference answer was supplied. No missing output was filled in.

numerical_agreement.application: Identity strings, formulas and atom/bond counts were compared exactly. No paired physical measurements or independently retrieved coordinate sets were supplied, so no numerical tolerance test or propagated cross-artifact coordinate comparison is applicable.

provenance.other_interface_provenance: Key-resolution interfaces query PubChem according to their supplied contracts, but their outputs expose no fetch/cache timestamps or response hashes. The MOL is an RDKit-reserialized database record.

comparisons.basis: Both SMILES produce exactly the same standard InChI. The database-returned InChI regenerates the original exact InChIKey.

results.decision: The name-to-structure-to-key-to-database round-trip passes exact formula, standard InChI and InChIKey checks. The differing SMILES strings encode the same identity. The retrieved CAS is consistent with that identity, but exhaustive CAS unambiguity remains unverified.
limitations: No timestamps or hashes were returned for CAS or key-resolution responses; none are inferred.
No MOL artifact hash was supplied or calculated. Its exact returned text is preserved by observation reference.

expected_answer.conclusion: The complete finite 4×80 native descriptor cohort has 48 all-zero columns. Cohort population standardization followed by two-PC PCA retains 85.47% of variance; seed42 k-means partitions M0/M1 from M2/M3. The independently constructed score sample covariance reconciles with PCA explained variances within tolerance. These are computational, descriptive results only, with no validated predictive or experimental interpretation.

clustering.label_ambiguity: Swapping labels 0 and 1 describes the same partition.
clustering.method: Euclidean k-means on the actual unrounded two-PC scores; k=2, n_init=10, random_state=42.

analysis.native_vector_precision: All coordinates below preserve the precision returned by the descriptor tool. No unavailable internal precision is claimed.

pca.method: Full-SVD PCA fitted to the standardized cohort, with two components and no additional scaling.
pca.total_variance_derivation: 32 nonconstant standardized columns each have population variance 1 and sample variance 4/3; constant columns contribute zero.

analysis.protocol: For each SMILES, the supplied implementation uses Chem.MolFromSmiles, AllChem.EmbedMolecule(mol, randomSeed=42), and rdMolDescriptors.CalcAUTOCORR3D(mol). It embeds the heavy-atom molecule without adding H; no geometry optimization is present in the supplied implementation. These are computed descriptors of generated conformations, not measured geometries or experimental autocorrelation.

comparison.interpretation: Sample covariance uses denominator 3, matching PCA explained-variance convention. Eigenvalues are sorted ascending by the eigensolver and descending by PCA. Component sign changes do not change variances or Euclidean clustering.

score_sample_covariance.construction: Center the four actual two-coordinate score rows, then compute C_ab = sum_i (s_ia-mean_a)(s_ib-mean_b)/(4-1). The score means are zero to floating-point precision. The covariance passed to the eigensolver was rounded to eight decimal places; the off-diagonal rounds to zero.

standardization.fit_population: The same four descriptive objects, in M0–M3 order; no held-out population.
standardization.formula: mu_j = sum_i x_ij / 4; sigma_j = sqrt(sum_i (x_ij-mu_j)^2 / 4); z_ij = (x_ij-mu_j)/scale_j, with scale_j=1 when sigma_j=0.

decision.grouping: The descriptive partition is {M0, M1} versus {M2, M3}. It is interpretable as proximity in this cohort-standardized two-PC representation, not as an established chemical taxonomy.
decision.numerical_reconciliation: The score-covariance eigenvalues agree with the two PCA explained variances within the supplied tolerances, including the explicitly reported covariance rounding.

limitations: Only four objects are present. Centered data have rank at most three, so this high-dimensional panel cannot establish stable or generalizable groups.
Means, scales, PCA and clustering all use the same descriptive cohort. This is not independent validation.
Two PCs retain about 85.47% of standardized variance; clustering omits the remaining variance.
Population standardization gives each nonconstant coordinate equal marginal variance. Correlated or redundant descriptor coordinates can still disproportionately affect distances.
Generated seed42 heavy-atom conformations omit explicit H and do not represent measured structures, conformational ensembles or experimental autocorrelation.
The eigensolver received an independently constructed covariance rounded to eight decimal places, rather than a full-precision covariance artifact.
No experimental or predictive validation is established by this descriptive teaching panel.

question: 3D autocorrelation descriptor cohort. Obtain the full native descriptor vector for each of the four supplied molecules in declared order. Construct the complete four-row numeric feature matrix; report its dimension and any non-finite entries. Fit per-coordinate population standardization to this descriptive cohort, with scale one for constant columns, then project to two principal components and cluster the actual scores into two groups with seed42. Independently construct the sample covariance of those two scores and obtain its symmetric eigenvalues; reconcile them with the two PCA explained variances, allowing sign/label ambiguity. Report retained variance, membership by molecule, zero-variance columns and whether grouping is interpretable on only four objects. This implementation embeds seed42 heavy-atom molecules without adding H. Report that exact protocol; no measured geometries or experimental autocorrelation. Use only actual successful observations, preserve sample identity and complete vector precision, and report the numerical intermediates, comparison and limitations. No experimental or predictive validation is established by this descriptive teaching panel.

workflow_goal: 3D autocorrelation descriptor cohort: Obtain the full native descriptor vector for each of the four supplied molecules in declared order. Construct the complete four-row numeric feature matrix; report its dimension and any non-finite entries. Fit per-coordinate population standardization to this descriptive cohort, with scale one for constant columns, then project to two principal components and cluster the actual scores into two groups with seed42. Independently construct the sample covariance of those two scores and obtain its symmetric eigenvalues; reconcile them with the two PCA explained variances, allowing sign/label ambiguity. Report retained variance, membership by molecule, zero-variance columns and whether grouping is interpretable on only four objects. This implementation embeds seed42 heavy-atom molecules without adding H. Report that exact protocol; no measured geometries or experimental autocorrelation.

expected_answer.conclusion: The complete finite 4×80 native descriptor cohort yields two PCs retaining 94.79% of standardized variance and the seed-42 partition {CCCCO, CCN(CC)CC} versus {CC(=O)O, c1ccoc1}. Independently constructed score covariance eigenvalues agree with PCA explained variances within tolerance. This is a numerically consistent descriptive teaching example, not a validated chemical grouping or predictive result.

clustering.method: Euclidean k-means on the actual two-dimensional PCA scores; k=2, n_init=10, random_state=42.

pca.method: Centered full-SVD PCA of the standardized cohort, without further scaling; two components.

analysis.protocol: For each SMILES, Chem.MolFromSmiles constructs the molecule; AllChem.EmbedMolecule(mol, randomSeed=42) embeds it without adding H; rdMolDescriptors.CalcAUTOCORR3D(mol) returns the native descriptor vector. These are computed descriptors of seed-42 heavy-atom embeddings, not measured geometries or experimental autocorrelation. No geometry optimization is performed in the supplied implementation.

comparison.interpretation: Agreement follows because PCA score sample covariance is diagonal with the retained PCA explained variances. Population scaling uses divisor 4, whereas PCA explained variance and this score covariance use divisor 3. Component signs and cluster labels are arbitrary and do not alter this agreement or the partition.
comparison.matching: Compare ascending covariance eigenvalues with reversed PCA explained variances.

score_covariance_check.construction: Independently form the two score-column means, subtract them, sum the outer products of the four centered score rows, and divide by n-1 = 3. The means and cross-covariance are zero up to floating-point roundoff.
score_covariance_check.precision_note: The symmetric eigensolver received this rounded covariance; the native descriptor matrix and scores used for PCA and clustering were not rounded.

standardization.fit_basis: All four objects in this descriptive cohort; the same cohort is transformed.
standardization.formula: mean_j = sum_i X_ij/4; scale_j = sqrt(sum_i (X_ij-mean_j)^2/4), replaced by 1 for constant columns; Z_ij = (X_ij-mean_j)/scale_j.

zero_variance_columns.description: All these columns are identically zero. The remaining 32 columns have positive cohort variance.

decision.grouping: The descriptive partition is {M0, M3} versus {M1, M2}, regardless of numeric label swaps.
decision.interpretability: The grouping can be described within this panel: M0 and M3 have nonzero coordinates 3–4 of each ten-coordinate block, whereas M1 and M2 have zeros there. It is not evidence for general chemical classes or a validated structure–property relationship.
decision.numerical_consistency: The covariance eigenvalues reconcile with both PCA explained variances within the supplied tolerances.

limitations: Only four objects support the analysis; centered data have rank at most three despite 80 descriptor coordinates.
Forty-eight constant coordinates contribute no variance. Correlated or repeated native coordinates can emphasize redundant information even after per-coordinate standardization.
Scaling, PCA and clustering are cohort-dependent; there is no held-out assessment or demonstrated cluster stability.
One seed-42 embedding per heavy-atom molecule does not establish conformational robustness, measured geometry, or experimental autocorrelation.
The two-component projection discards about 5.21% of cohort variance; the requested clustering concerns projected scores, not the complete descriptor space.
No experimental or predictive validation is established by this descriptive teaching panel.

expected_answer.conclusion: The complete 4×11 displayed descriptor matrix is finite and has three constant columns. Cohort standardization followed by two-component PCA retains 83.86% of variance. Independent rounded-score sample covariance eigenvalues agree with PCA within the requested tolerances and propagated rounding. clustering.interpretation: Pyridine is the singleton group; ethanol, acetone and ethyl acetate form the other group. Cluster labels may be swapped without changing membership.
clustering.method: Euclidean k-means on the actual full-precision returned two-component scores; two clusters, ten initializations, seed 42.

analysis.descriptor_columns: EState-VSA bins 1 through 11, in native order

descriptor_rounding_comparison.propagation_scope: The eigenvalue check above propagates score-display rounding. It does not establish invariance of fitted standardization, PCA or clustering to hidden descriptor rounding.
descriptor_rounding_comparison.requested_tolerance_caution: The supplied atol+rtol·|d| is smaller than 0.00005 for every displayed descriptor here. Thus displayed values alone cannot certify agreement with hidden internal descriptors at the requested tolerance. No hidden-precision comparison or refit was available.
descriptor_rounding_comparison.statement: The matrix reproduces every displayed native bin exactly, without truncating the vector or changing row identity. For an underlying value x rounded to d, use |x−d|≤0.00005, rather than treating four printed decimals as full internal precision. For differences between two independently rounded entries, the worst-case error is 0.0001.
descriptor_rounding_comparison.units: No absolute unit convention is inferred from the tool output.

independent_score_covariance_check.audit_note: The earlier covariance approximation in o008 is superseded by the explicitly auditable rounded-score calculation in o009.

comparison.interpretation: Eigenvalues match the two PCA sample explained variances after descending-order alignment. Eigenvector signs and PCA component signs are arbitrary. The near-zero covariance off-diagonal agrees with orthogonal principal-component scores.
comparison.rounding_propagation: Each rounded score differs by at most 5e-7. Conservative covariance-entry error bounds are approximately 2.161e-6 and 1.705e-6 on the diagonals and 1.933e-6 off-diagonal; the resulting eigenvalue perturbation bound is approximately 4.094e-6. The observed discrepancies are consistent with this rounding.

independent_score_covariance_check.method: Independently calculate sample covariance with divisor 4−1=3 from the observed scores rounded to six decimals. Explicitly subtract the outer product of coordinate sums divided by 4 before dividing by 3.

standardization.definition: Fit coordinate means and population standard deviations to these four rows; use scale 1 for constant columns.
standardization.precision: All descriptor digits returned by the tool were preserved. The tool exposes four-decimal descriptors, not its internal unrounded values.

decision.summary: The two-component representation retains about 83.86% of standardized cohort variance. Its covariance eigenvalues reconcile with PCA, and seed-42 k-means isolates M2. This is a descriptive teaching result, not a validated molecular classification.

limitations: Only four objects are present; the centered feature matrix has rank at most three. Two components necessarily omit part of the cohort variation.
Means, scales, PCA and clusters were all fitted on the same descriptive cohort. There is no holdout set, experimental validation or predictive validation.
Population standardization gives each nonconstant coordinate equal marginal variance, including sparse bins; the observed partition depends on that choice and on projection to two components.
A singleton cluster and three-member cluster provide very little evidence about stability, generalization or chemical mechanisms.
All eleven native bins are available only as four-decimal tool output. Internal descriptor precision and hidden-precision sensitivity are not established.
The reported constant columns are constant in the returned matrix; no additional internal-precision measurement was available.

workflow_goal: EState-VSA descriptor cohort: Obtain the full native descriptor vector for each of the four supplied molecules in declared order. Construct the complete four-row numeric feature matrix; report its dimension and any non-finite entries. Fit per-coordinate population standardization to this descriptive cohort, with scale one for constant columns, then project to two principal components and cluster the actual scores into two groups with seed42. Independently construct the sample covariance of those two scores and obtain its symmetric eigenvalues; reconcile them with the two PCA explained variances, allowing sign/label ambiguity. Report retained variance, membership by molecule, zero-variance columns and whether grouping is interpretable on only four objects. All eleven native bins are printed to four decimals. Compare the displayed vectors with propagated rounding; do not invent absolute unit conventions.
